findings.F1: The day after a coin's daily move, its next-day return runs against that move, with a regression slope t of −3.62 in BTCUSD and −3.98 in ETHUSD (2,873 daily cases each); the lowest prior-day quintile is followed by +0.44% and the highest by −0.06% to −0.14% (Welch t 2.27 and 1.91).
findings.F2: This next-day reversal is concentrated in the highest 20-day-volatility tercile, with a slope of −0.0070 per standardised prior move (t −5.82, n 1,612); the middle tercile shows none (t −0.06) and the lowest tercile leans to slight continuation (+0.0015, t 2.15).
findings.F3: The reversal slope is negative in every year from 2018 to 2025, and is strongest in 2020 (t −5.19, n 720) and 2021 (t −2.13).
findings.F4: The book's gain comes almost entirely from days held long, which average +0.26% a day over 2,920 days against +0.003% over 2,864 days held short; short trades net only +0.27% (BTC) and +0.88% (ETH) per trade against +4.5% and +5.2% for long trades.
findings.F5: The tested 7-day continuation is weak beside the 1-day reversal. The forecast quintiles rise monotonically in 7-day excess return, from −1.33% to +1.54%, but no quintile reaches |t| 2, and the sign-weighted excess falls to +0.2% in 2023 and −0.35% in 2024 (about 102 cases each).

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily volatility is high, the larger its one-day return measured in units of its own 20-day daily volatility, the more its return over the next 1 day runs in the opposite direction.
ideas.consequence: In volatile stretches a trader would refuse to chase a large daily move and would lean against it for the following day, more so the larger the move.
ideas.name: high-volatility next-day reversal

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's own 20-day daily volatility, the more strongly its return over the next 1 day runs opposite to its return over the past 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would let a coin's recent volatility set how hard to fade its last day's move, fading it most when volatility is highest.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled daily reversal
